review_notes: I read all of CapVal.lean (lines 1–90). I grepped every use of capVal in the RegtsSevenster tree. The file has no @[simp] attributes and defines one noncomputable def (capVal) with three lemmas about it (capVal_zero, capVal_sum, capVal_smul). All downstream uses (CapClosed, CapExpansion, MasterSum) apply these lemmas with explicit `rw`, and capVal_succ in CapPeelSplit is also used with `rw`. I found no use where a missing simp lemma forces a manual workaround. capVal_sum and capVal_smul could be repackaged as a bundled linear map so that map_sum and map_smul fire, but I found no concrete use that would benefit. Tagging capVal_zero @[simp] would be untested: its statement relies on `(superPow _ 0).even` being defeq to ℂ, and its LHS has implicit-argument-heavy structure. There is also no competing rule and no credible rewrite cycle, because the definition is not marked simp and the lemmas orient toward distributing capVal. I made no simp-interface claim from this file. The remaining uncertainty is that I did not inspect every simp-set interaction in files that do not mention capVal.
